elements.quote: The aim of this review is to compare a removable orthosis versus a cast regarding safety and functional outcome in the NOM of stable type B ankle fractures.
elements.reason: The abstract identifies the study as a review (systematic review and meta-analysis is also stated).

elements.quote: The aim of this review is to compare a removable orthosis versus a cast regarding safety and functional outcome in the NOM of stable type B ankle fractures.
elements.reason: An explicit main objective/comparison question is stated.
The abstract does not specify the main inclusion and exclusion criteria.
No information sources and no 'last searched' dates are reported in the abstract.

elements.quote: The methodological quality of the included studies was assessed with the methodological index for non-randomized studies instrument.
elements.reason: Risk/methodological quality assessment method is explicitly named.

elements.quote: A meta-analysis showed statistically significant higher odds of developing complications in the cast group [odds ratio (OR), 4.67 (95% confidence interval (CI) 1.52-14.35)]. Functional outcome in OMAS did not vary significantly at 6 weeks, mean difference (MD) - 6.64 (95% CI - 13.72 to + 0.45), and at 12 weeks, MD - 6.91 (95% CI - 18.73 to + 4.91).
elements.reason: The abstract specifies that meta-analysis was performed and provides the synthesis effect metrics used.

elements.quote: Results Five studies were included. Two were randomized clinical trials, and three were observational studies, including a total of 516 patients.
elements.reason: Total number of included studies and participants, plus study-type characteristics, are reported.

elements.quote: A meta-analysis showed statistically significant higher odds of developing complications in the cast group [odds ratio (OR), 4.67 (95% confidence interval (CI) 1.52-14.35)]. Functional outcome in OMAS did not vary significantly at 6 weeks, mean difference (MD) - 6.64 (95% CI - 13.72 to + 0.45), and at 12 weeks, MD - 6.91 (95% CI - 18.73 to + 4.91). The mean difference of functional outcome in OMAS at 26 weeks or longer was significantly better in the removable orthosis group; MD - 2.63 (95% CI - 5.01 to - 0.25).
elements.reason: Main outcomes and their results (with effect sizes and CIs) are presented for complications and functional outcome at multiple time points.

elements.quote: A meta-analysis showed statistically significant higher odds of developing complications in the cast group [odds ratio (OR), 4.67 (95% confidence interval (CI) 1.52-14.35)]. Functional outcome in OMAS did not vary significantly at 6 weeks, mean difference (MD) - 6.64 (95% CI - 13.72 to + 0.45), and at 12 weeks, MD - 6.91 (95% CI - 18.73 to + 4.91). The mean difference of functional outcome in OMAS at 26 weeks or longer was significantly better in the removable orthosis group; MD - 2.63 (95% CI - 5.01 to - 0.25).
elements.reason: Because a meta-analysis was conducted, the summary estimates and 95% CIs are reported.

elements.quote: A meta-analysis showed statistically significant higher odds of developing complications in the cast group [odds ratio (OR), 4.67 (95% confidence interval (CI) 1.52-14.35)]. ... The mean difference of functional outcome in OMAS at 26 weeks or longer was significantly better in the removable orthosis group; MD - 2.63 (95% CI - 5.01 to - 0.25).
elements.reason: The direction of effect and which group is favored are described (cast favored for lower complications is not; removable orthosis favored for 26+ weeks functional outcome).
No limitations of the included evidence (e.g., risk of bias, inconsistency, imprecision) are reported in the abstract.

elements.quote: Conclusion Results of this systematic review and meta-analysis show that a removable orthosis is a safe alternative type of NOM, as complication numbers are significantly lower in the orthosis group. In addition, no statistically significant differences were found in terms of functional outcome between a removable orthosis and a cast at 6 and 12 weeks.
elements.reason: The abstract provides a general interpretation and implications for practice.
The abstract does not specify the primary source of funding for the review.
The abstract does not provide any register name or registration number.

elements.quote: Purpose There is currently no consensus on nonoperative management in adult patients after a stable type B ankle fracture.
elements.reason: The review’s rationale is grounded in the current state of knowledge by explicitly stating there is no consensus on nonoperative management for stable type B ankle fractures.

elements.quote: The aim of this review is to compare a removable orthosis versus a cast regarding safety and functional outcome in the NOM of stable type B ankle fractures.
elements.reason: The need to conduct the review is explained through the stated aim to resolve safety and functional outcome uncertainty by comparing the two nonoperative approaches.
No specific prior similar systematic review(s) are identified and cited in the retrieved evidence as the basis for why an updated/current review is needed.

elements.quote: Removable orthoses have proven their value in the recovery process of other fractures of the long bones, and are increasingly suggested as an alternative to a cast for stable type B fractures [16, 17]. Orthoses can be taken off, allowing early (weight-bearing) mobilization, potentially preventing the consequences of rigid immobilization and accelerating recovery [16, 18].
elements.reason: For an intervention-effect review, the retrieved evidence describes a hypothesised mechanism: removable orthoses enable early mobilization, may prevent consequences of rigid immobilization, and can accelerate recovery.
The retrieved evidence does not report a logic model or any diagrammatic logic model showing hypothesised relationships between intervention components and outcomes.

elements.quote: Purpose There is currently no consensus on nonoperative management in adult patients after a stable type B ankle fracture. The aim of this review is to compare a removable orthosis versus a cast regarding safety and functional outcome in the NOM of stable type B ankle fractures.
elements.reason: The review objective is explicitly stated as an aim (compare removable orthosis vs cast for safety and functional outcome), but it is not formulated as a clear research question using a specific question-formulation framework.

elements.quote: The aim of this review is to compare a removable orthosis versus a cast regarding safety and functional outcome in the NOM of stable type B ankle fractures.
elements.reason: The planned comparison between interventions (removable orthosis vs cast) is stated, but full PICO details (e.g., explicit population eligibility phrased for PICO, and specific outcome definitions mapped into PICO) are not provided in the excerpt.

elements.quote: Studies were included if: (1) NOM with a cast versus removable orthosis after stable type B ankle fractures were compared, (2) included patients were skeletally mature (16 years or older), (3) complications (e.g. DVT, stiffness) and functional outcome measured in Patient Reported Outcome Measures (PROMs) up to 52 weeks were described, (4) available in Dutch, English, or German, (5) original data was reported (no reviews, editorial letters, or expert opinions).
elements.reason: The evidence specifies key study characteristics used for eligibility (comparison/participants and a follow-up requirement of PROMs up to 52 weeks), but it does not clearly specify all items required by the criterion (e.g., eligible study designs and settings are not explicitly listed as eligibility criteria).

elements.quote: Studies were included if: ... (4) available in Dutch, English, or German, (5) original data was reported (no reviews, editorial letters, or expert opinions).
elements.reason: Language and report/publication type (original data vs reviews/editorials/expert opinions) are specified, but dissemination year and publication/report status beyond 'original data' are not explicitly described.
No evidence was retrieved describing how exclusions are distinguished based on whether outcomes were not measured versus outcome results not reported.

elements.quote: A total of 303 patients were immobilized with a cast versus 213 patients treated with an orthosis.
elements.reason: The review’s synthesis groups corresponding to the defined comparison are explicitly described as 'cast' versus 'orthosis/removable orthosis' for included studies.
Although eligibility restrictions are listed, no retrieved evidence provides rationales for notable restrictions on study eligibility.

elements.quote: A systematic PubMed, Embase and Cochrane literature search was conducted on the 15th of July 2022.
elements.reason: Reports the last search/consultation date (15th of July 2022) for the information sources searched (PubMed, Embase, Cochrane).

elements.quote: A systematic PubMed, Embase and Cochrane literature search was conducted on the 15th of July 2022.
elements.reason: Provides the database names and the search date, but does not report coverage dates or details of the search interface/platform/coverage for each database.

No study registers/regulatory databases/online repositories (beyond the databases and additional databanks mentioned separately for websites) are reported as being searched with their names/date restrictions.

elements.quote: If full-texts were not obtained via PubMed or the journal of publication and the author of the article had not been reached, the additional databanks from Google Scholar and Research Gate were searched.
elements.reason: Names Google Scholar and Research Gate as additional searched sources, but does not provide URLs and no date restrictions for these sources are reported.
No organisations or manufacturers contacted to identify studies are named in the retrieved evidence.

elements.quote: Contact with the corresponding author was attempted for missing data.
elements.reason: Describes a type of individual contacted (corresponding authors) but does not indicate they were contacted to identify studies (the excerpt only states contact for missing data).

elements.quote: Reference checking was performed to search for additional relevant studies.
elements.reason: Indicates that reference lists were examined, but does not specify the types of reference lists examined (e.g., bibliographies of included studies, forward/backward citations).
No details are provided about backward/forward citation searching (seed reports, citation index/platform, or search date).
No journals or conference proceedings consulted are described with source names, dates covered, and search methods in the retrieved evidence.

elements.quote: Search syntax used in PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane to identify eligible studies for a systematic review of type B ankle fractures comparing removable orthosis and a cast as nonoperative management Pubmed: 15th July 2022
elements.reason: The manuscript provides some search syntax information in Appendix 1 for PubMed (including the date), but the retrieved evidence does not show the complete full search strategies “as actually run” for every listed source (e.g., Embase and Cochrane).

elements.quote: All relevant synonyms for two search terms, 'ankle fracture' and 'orthosis' were included in the search syntax (Appendix 1). Studies were included if: ... (4) available in Dutch, English, or German
elements.reason: Eligibility-related constraints (e.g., language availability) are stated, but the retrieved evidence does not provide a clear description of all search limits used (e.g., database filters/limits) and how each limit is justified by reference to eligibility criteria.
No retrieved evidence describes published search approaches/filters, citations for filters, or any adaptations.
No retrieved evidence specifies any NLP/text-analysis tools used to refine search terms.
No retrieved evidence specifies tools used to translate/convert search strings between sources.
No retrieved evidence describes validation of the search strategy (process or validation studies).
No retrieved evidence describes peer review of the search strategy (process, tool such as PRESS, or similar).

The retrieved evidence does not indicate that the search structure deviated from a standard concept-based approach such that a final conceptual structure and its explorations would be required. Therefore, there is insufficient evidence to consider this applicable in this submission.

Studies identified from: PubMed(n=1479) Embase (n=2081) Cochrane (n=81)
Duplicate studies removed (n=1367)
Studies screened (n=2274)
Studies sought for retrieval (n=20)

Studies included in systematic review meta-analysis (n=5)
elements.reason: The PRISMA flow diagram reports the numbers of records/studies at each screening stage (screened, sought for retrieval, assessed for eligibility, and included).

elements.quote: Screening for relevance by title, abstract and full text before final inclusion has been performed by two independent researchers (JS and TN).
elements.reason: The manuscript explicitly states that two independent researchers (JS and TN) performed screening for relevance across title, abstract, and full text.

elements.quote: Disagreements were resolved by discussion with a third reviewer (DS) until consensus was reached.
elements.reason: The process for resolving screening disagreements is described (discussion with a third reviewer until consensus).
No process is described for obtaining or confirming eligibility information from study investigators.
There is no description of methods to translate abstracts or full articles for eligibility assessment.
Although Rayyan is mentioned for data management, no integration of automation tools into the selection process is described.
The provided evidence does not mention externally derived classifiers, their versions/references, or pre-screen removals via such classifiers.
The provided evidence does not mention internally derived classifiers or their training/validation.
The provided evidence does not mention machine-learning prioritisation tools or screening stopping/prioritisation rules.

The evidence does not report the number of reviewers collecting data from each report (data extraction team size per included study).
Although the text states that screening was performed by two independent researchers, it does not state whether multiple data collectors extracted data independently from each report.

elements.quote: Disagreements were resolved by discussion with a third reviewer (DS) until consensus was reached.
elements.reason: A disagreement-resolution process is described, but the surrounding context is methodological quality assessment (MINORS) rather than explicit data extraction disagreements between data collectors.

elements.quote: Contact with the corresponding author was attempted for missing data. Additional data was successfully obtained from van den Berg et al. [23].
elements.reason: The authors describe contacting corresponding authors to obtain/confirm missing data, including a successful example.

elements.quote: Rayyan was used for data management and selection of the studies [20].
elements.reason: Rayyan is reported as a tool used for data management/selection, but the evidence does not describe automation tools for data collection/extraction, or any training/validation of such tools.
No methods for translating articles for data collection are described in the retrieved evidence.
No software used to extract data from figures is reported in the retrieved evidence.
No decision rules for selecting data from multiple reports or resolving inconsistencies are provided in the retrieved evidence.

elements.quote: The safety of NOM during posttraumatic care management was evaluated using the reported number of complications up to one year after injury. Complications of NOM consisted of persistent joint stiffness, pressure injuries caused by orthosis, or casts (epidermal excoriation, dermal excoriation), persistent pain [Visual Analogue Scale (VAS) lower than 3], persistent perceived instability at final follow-up, failure of immobilization material (e.g. breakage), or clinically diagnosed DVT.
elements.reason: The evidence defines a safety/complications outcome domain (and specifies what complications include). However, it does not clearly state that all outcome domains for which data were sought are comprehensively listed and defined.

elements.quote: The safety of NOM during posttraumatic care management was evaluated using the reported number of complications up to one year after injury.
elements.reason: A measurement time frame is specified for the safety/complications outcome domain (up to one year).
No statement is provided about whether all compatible results within each outcome domain were sought (or how compatibility/all-results decisions were handled).
Although time points are discussed for functional outcomes, there is no explicit description of a selection process used when not all compatible results were sought within outcome domains.
No information is reported about changes to outcome-domain inclusion/definitions/importance with rationales.
No information is reported about changes to the process for selecting results within eligible outcome domains with rationales.

elements.quote: For the secondary outcome, functional outcome, 12 weeks follow-up was considered the most appropriate timing for measuring OMAS.
elements.reason: The evidence indicates that (for the functional outcome) a specific time point (12 weeks) was considered most appropriate. However, it does not clearly report which outcomes were prioritized overall for interpreting conclusions or provide the full rationale for prioritization.

elements.quote: Extracted patient-related data were: included number of patients, age in years, sex of included patients, number of patients treated with a removable orthosis, type of orthosis (e.g. walker, air-stirrup brace), number of patients treated with a cast, duration of NOM in weeks (e.g. immobilization in cast in weeks). Extracted diagnostic criteria to assess fracture stability were extracted: type of diagnostics (radiograph, CT, ultrasound), classification system (Lauge-Hansen, Weber), sub-classification (Supination External Rotation type II, Weber B), additional radiological criteria [Superior Clear Space (SCS) in millimetre (mm)], Medial Clear Space (MCS) in mm, MCS and SCS ratio, fibular dislocation in mm, MCS under external rotation stress in mm, additional clinical diagnostic criteria (e.g. medial side tenderness), time to performance diagnostics in days (e.g. at primary visit, or 10-14 days after trauma). The following weight-bearing related data were extracted: weight-bearing permission by a medical specialist (yes/no), percentage of allowed weight-bearing in the affected limb (0-100), time to start weight-bearing after injury in days, reported number and type of complications, including Confidence Intervals (CI) or, if CIs are unavailable p values, used scale and timing of reported functional outcomes (e.g. PROMs, including CIs and p values).
elements.reason: The review lists and defines multiple categories of data extracted (patient-related, diagnostic criteria, weight-bearing, complications, and functional outcomes), indicating that other sought variables were specified.

elements.quote: To perform a meta-analysis, missing means or SDs that were not reported in an article and which could not be retrieved after the attempt to contact the corresponding author were estimated if possible using the available information. If the range was available for outcome variables, the SD was estimated as range divided by 4 [27]. The SD was estimated from the standard error (SE) using the formula SE = SD/√ n , where n is the sample size. The SE was estimated from the 95% CI by dividing the width of the CI by 2 × 1.96 = 3.92 [27].
elements.reason: The manuscript describes assumptions/approaches for handling missing or unretrievable information (estimating missing means/SDs using range, SE, or 95% CI formulas).
No evidence was retrieved showing any specific tool used to determine which data items to collect (e.g., a pilot-tested extraction form, guideline, or checklist) in the provided excerpts.

elements.quote: Two independent researchers (JS and TN) assessed the methodological quality according to the Methodological Index for Non-Randomized Studies (MINORS) for all full-texts of included studies [21].
elements.reason: The risk-of-bias tool used (MINORS) is specified, but no tool version is reported.
The evidence does not report the domains/components/items assessed by the MINORS tool.

elements.quote: For this review, a score of less than 14 was considered poor quality, 15-19 moderate quality, and 20-24 for good quality for comparative studies [22].
elements.reason: Rules for classifying methodological quality based on the MINORS score are reported, but it is not explicitly stated as an overall risk-of-bias judgement or the exact rules used to derive it.
No adaptations to an existing risk-of-bias tool are described in the retrieved evidence.
The retrieved evidence reports use of the MINORS tool but does not describe any newly developed risk-of-bias tool; therefore, this element does not apply based on the available information.

elements.quote: Two independent researchers (JS and TN) assessed the methodological quality according to the Methodological Index for Non-Randomized Studies (MINORS)... Disagreements were resolved by discussion with a third reviewer (DS) until consensus was reached.
elements.reason: Number of reviewers (two), their independence, and the disagreement-resolution procedure (discussion with a third reviewer DS until consensus) are explicitly reported.
The evidence describes contacting the corresponding author for missing data, but it does not specify processes for obtaining or confirming risk-of-bias information from study investigators.
No automation tools for risk-of-bias assessment are mentioned in the retrieved evidence.

elements.quote: A pooled odds ratio (OR) was estimated for dichotomous outcomes. The Mantel-Haenszel statistical method was used to construct a 95% CI [28]. The data of OMAS are presented as mean between-group difference (with 95% confidence interval).
elements.reason: The review specifies effect measures by outcome type: pooled odds ratio (OR) for dichotomous outcomes and mean between-group difference (MD) for OMAS (continuous functional outcome).

elements.quote: A mean clinically important difference (MCID) was set at 4.4 points on the OMAS scale as suggested by Nilsson et al. [29].
elements.reason: A threshold (MCID) of 4.4 points for OMAS is reported, including a citation indicating rationale/source.
No methods are reported describing re-expression of synthesized results using another effect measure.
No justification is provided for the choice of effect measure.

elements.quote: Rayyan was used for data management and selection of the studies [20]. After the removal of duplicates, titles and abstracts were screened for relevance. If full-texts were not obtained via PubMed or the journal of publication and the author of the article had not been reached, the additional databanks from Google Scholar and Research Gate were searched. Obtained full-texts of eligible studies were read before final inclusion. Screening for relevance by title, abstract and full text before final inclusion has been performed by two independent researchers (JS and TN). Reference checking was performed to search for additional relevant studies.
elements.reason: The review describes the processes used to decide study eligibility (duplicate removal; title/abstract screening; full-text retrieval and reading; independent screening by two researchers; and reference checking), including the tools/databases used for selection.

elements.quote: To perform a meta-analysis, missing means or SDs that were not reported in an article and which could not be retrieved after the attempt to contact the corresponding author were estimated if possible using the available information. If the range was available for outcome variables, the SD was estimated as range divided by 4 [27]. The SD was estimated from the standard error (SE) using the formula SE = SD/√ n , where n is the sample size. The SE was estimated from the 95% CI by dividing the width of the CI by 2 × 1.96 = 3.92 [27]. Data were converted into the same units if needed.
elements.reason: The Methods describe how missing summary statistics (means/SDs) were estimated when not reported and how data were converted into consistent units for synthesis.

elements.quote: Data management, statistical analyses, and graphical representation were performed using Review Manager software (RevMan v 5.4.1) provided by the Cochrane Collaboration [26].
elements.reason: The software used for data handling/outputs is stated, but there is no description of the specific tabular structures used to display results of individual studies and syntheses or the data included in those tables.

elements.quote: Data management, statistical analyses, and graphical representation were performed using Review Manager software (RevMan v 5.4.1) provided by the Cochrane Collaboration [26].
elements.reason: The review states that graphical representation was performed using RevMan, but it does not describe the graphical methods (e.g., types of plots/figures) used to display results of individual studies and syntheses.
No evidence was found describing any basis for ordering or grouping studies within tables or graphs.
No evidence was found reporting the rationale for using non-standard graphs.

elements.quote: Data management, statistical analyses, and graphical representation were performed using Review Manager software (RevMan v 5.4.1) provided by the Cochrane Collaboration [26].
elements.reason: Reports the statistical software used and its version (RevMan v 5.4.1).
No alternative synthesis or summary method is described for situations where meta-analysis was not possible.

elements.quote: The random-effects model was used for meta-analyses.
elements.reason: The model (random-effects) is stated, but a rationale for the choice is not provided in the retrieved evidence.

elements.quote: The inverse variance statistical method was used to construct a 95% CI. A pooled odds ratio (OR) was estimated for dichotomous outcomes. The Mantel-Haenszel statistical method was used to construct a 95% CI [28].
elements.reason: States the statistical methods used for summary effects/confidence intervals (inverse variance; Mantel-Haenszel for dichotomous outcomes; pooled OR).

elements.quote: The assessment of statistical heterogeneity was performed by estimating statistical measures of heterogeneity: Cochran Q (Chi-square test), I 2 , and τ 2 (tau-square).
elements.reason: Specifies the measures used to identify/quantify statistical heterogeneity (Cochran Q, I², τ²).
Does not report the between-study variance estimator used for random-effects meta-analysis in the retrieved evidence.

elements.quote: The inverse variance statistical method was used to construct a 95% CI. ... The Mantel-Haenszel statistical method was used to construct a 95% CI [28].
elements.reason: Provides the method used to calculate 95% confidence intervals for the summary effect.
Other random-effects implementation details (e.g., specific estimation approach/settings) are not reported in the retrieved evidence.
The retrieved evidence describes random-effects meta-analysis, but provides no indication of Bayesian meta-analysis; therefore the Bayesian-specific item does not apply based on the evidence.
No method is described for accounting for statistical dependency among multiple estimates from the same study.
No planned syntheses judged impossible or inappropriate are identified and no reasons are provided in the retrieved evidence.

elements.quote: The assessment of statistical heterogeneity was performed by estimating statistical measures of heterogeneity: Cochran Q (Chi-square test), I 2 , and τ 2 (tau-square). The random-effects model was used for meta-analyses.
elements.reason: The evidence reports how heterogeneity was assessed, but does not describe methods used to explore possible causes of heterogeneity (e.g., subgroup analysis or meta-regression).

elements.quote:
To perform a meta-analysis, missing means or SDs that were not reported in an article and which could not be retrieved after the attempt to contact the corresponding author were estimated if possible using the available information.

If the range was available for outcome variables, the SD was estimated as range divided by 4 [27]. The SD was estimated from the standard error (SE) using the formula SE = SD/√ n , where n is the sample size. The SE was estimated from the 95% CI by dividing the width of the CI by 2 × 1.96 = 3.92 [27].
elements.reason: The review explicitly identifies estimated/computed values (missing means/SDs/SE derived from ranges or CIs) rather than only directly reported data.

elements.quote: A meta-analysis showed statistically significant higher odds of developing complications in the cast group [odds ratio (OR), 4.67 (95% confidence interval (CI) 1.52-14.35)]. Functional outcome in OMAS did not vary significantly at 6 weeks, mean difference (MD) - 6.64 (95% CI - 13.72 to + 0.45), and at 12 weeks, MD - 6.91 (95% CI - 18.73 to + 4.91). The mean difference of functional outcome in OMAS at 26 weeks or longer was significantly better in the removable orthosis group; MD - 2.63 (95% CI - 5.01 to - 0.25).

elements.quote: This study has several limitations that need to be addressed. First, selection bias may have been introduced because of the heterogeneity in the used classification systems, diagnostic methods and criteria to exclude additional medial or posterior injury. This may have led to an incorrect selection of patients with a 'true' Lauge-Hansen ankle fracture. Recently two reviews aimed to pinpoint one optimal strategy to exclude medial or posterior injury in stable type B ankle fractures, but no consensus has been reached [10, 49]. Second, the small number of studies, with relatively small sample sizes, conducted on this issue reduces the generalizability of findings. Last, the length of followup and timing of OMAS varied across studies and affected functional outcome as they were measured at different stages of healing.
elements.reason: The Discussion includes explicit limitations of the included evidence (selection bias from heterogeneity, small number of studies/small sample sizes, and variation in follow-up length/timing of OMAS affecting functional outcomes).

elements.quote:
Future research should focus on developing a practical, more sensitive and specific technique to exclude additional medial or posterior injury.

To increase the comparability of future studies, a more uniform design in terms of classification systems, endpoints of follow-up, and short-term and long-term outcomes to evaluate ankle fractures should be used.

Furthermore, limited evidence on the optimal rigidity of removable orthosis exists, and should be further investigated to optimize NOM after stable type B ankle fractures.
